note: Reported defects from the engagement brief are tracked as hypotheses. Status reflects what has been reproduced/fixed against the current working tree, not the audited baseline. Live gates are BLOCKED, never PASSED, without an authorized workspace.

findings.title: Malformed name/schedule YAML breaks the whole bundle
findings.evidence: Line 187 collapsed `schedule:` onto the `name:` value line for the formula_prioritization job. `yaml.safe_load_all` fails at line 187: 'expected <block end>, but found <scalar>'. A single unparseable resource file means `databricks bundle validate/deploy` cannot load any job.
findings.fix: Split the `name` and `schedule` keys onto separate lines with correct indentation.

findings.title: Duplicate YAML keys silently override jobs/pipelines
findings.evidence: A duplicate mapping key is silently accepted by a plain safe_load, so a second job under an existing key would erase the first. Checked with a duplicate-rejecting loader across all bundle files.
findings.fix: No duplicate keys present in current tree; guard added to prevent regression.

findings.title: Referenced notebook paths must all resolve
findings.evidence: 133 notebook_path references checked against the filesystem; 0 missing.

findings.title: Setup notebooks must be re-runnable as idempotent upgrades without data loss
findings.evidence: The platform has no separate migration tool; the setup notebooks are both the clean install and the upgrade path. Audited their DDL: all CREATE TABLE use IF NOT EXISTS (175 idempotent statements), existing-deployment column upgrades use ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMNS IF NOT EXISTS (e.g. response_actions finding_id/approved_finding_revision), and there is no CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE or DROP TABLE. The idempotent-upgrade property already holds; no new parallel migration hierarchy was added (would duplicate the existing pattern). A guard now locks the property.

findings.title: Deployed serverless notebooks use serverless-incompatible Spark APIs
findings.evidence: Deployment-aware audit mapped jobs whose environment spec sets environment_version (serverless) to the notebooks they deploy, then scanned those files. Four deployed serverless notebooks used APIs serverless does not expose (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/serverless/limitations): streaming_correlation, temporal_window_correlator and graph_neighborhood used spark.sparkContext.broadcast; trend_engine_cet used spark.sparkContext.setCheckpointDir and imports GraphFrames (a JVM library, absent from its serverless dependency list).
findings.regression: tests/contract/test_serverless_notebook_apis.py (now also flags hardcoded processingTime triggers and cache/persist/unpersist on serverless-deployed notebooks)
findings.fix: Replaced the three broadcast lookups with plain closure capture (Spark serializes captured Python objects to executors), which is semantically identical for the small baseline/projection maps and offline-verified clean. trend_engine_cet cannot be fixed by a Python edit: GraphFrames + RDD checkpointing require classic compute, so its serverless-to-classic migration is tracked as BLOCKED pending staging validation and allowlisted in the regression. Gate A completed the trend_engine_cet migration in-bundle: its job now runs on a dedicated classic cluster (cet_classic) with the GraphFrames Maven coordinate supplied via the graphframes_maven bundle variable, and temporal_window_correlator was likewise moved to a classic streaming cluster; graph_neighborhood_embeddings additionally had its cache() calls removed. Live staging validation of the classic runtime + GraphFrames coordinate remains pending an authorized workspace.

findings.title: Scheduled ingestion writer used uuid() instead of stable SDP IDs
findings.evidence: Prior session unified deterministic content-addressed IDs over Kafka coordinates across the streaming and durable paths.
findings.regression: tests/property/test_idempotency.py + tests/property/test_event_identity.py (native-id precedence, deterministic hash basis, payload disambiguation) + tests/contract/test_idempotent_persistence.py
findings.fix: Unified all raw-event id derivation onto notebooks/_shared/event_identity.derive_event_id (Bronze ingestion + realtime SDP), and switched Bronze event persistence from append+uuid() to an idempotent MERGE on the stable id.

findings.title: Producer/consumer signal-shape mismatch at canonical boundary
findings.evidence: Prior session added DETECTION_SIGNAL_COLUMNS/CLASSES and projected the evidence builder to the canonical shape. Gate B (B4) closed the CEP boundary, where cep_pattern_matches had THREE disagreeing shapes: the setup DDL, the producer (01_streaming_correlation_engine) and the UEO CEP lens (09) each expected different columns, and the producer explicitly DROPPED event_ids + mitre_tactic/mitre_technique before writing, destroying event lineage and MITRE attribution at the boundary; the UEO lens then read a matched_events column that no longer existed.
findings.regression: tests/contract/test_phase2_contracts.py + tests/contract/test_cep_signal_contract.py (contract covers every column the UEO reads; producer emits the canonical columns and does NOT strip lineage/MITRE; UEO lens reads event_ids and carries MITRE; DDL defines the canonical columns)
findings.fix: Added contracts.CEP_PATTERN_MATCH_COLUMNS + CEP_LINEAGE_FIELDS as the single source of truth. The producer now writes an explicit canonical schema that PRESERVES event_ids/mitre_tactic/mitre_technique (the drop-comprehension is gone); the setup DDL was expanded to match; and the UEO CEP lens now projects event_ids AS source_event_ids (was the nonexistent matched_events) and folds the MITRE technique into the explanation.

findings.title: Threat-intel match persisted before nonrecoverable alert emission
findings.evidence: Reported match-written/alert-missing recovery gap. The offline fault-injection regression cannot import the real logic: notebooks/detection/02_threat_intel_matching.py runs dbutils.widgets and spark.sql at module top level, so it is not importable without a live runtime. Reproducing this offline needs the match-persist/alert-emit step extracted into an importable _shared helper (a streaming-detector refactor) or a Databricks workspace; not attempted blind to preserve detector semantics.
findings.regression: tests/property/test_ti_recovery.py (fault-injection: crash between match and alert, crash between alert and mark, idempotent replay) + tests/contract/test_idempotent_persistence.py
findings.fix: Reframed match->alert as a durable obligation in notebooks/_shared/ti_recovery.py (pure, offline-testable) and mirrored it in notebooks/detection/02_threat_intel_matching.py: (1) MERGE findings on a deterministic id (indicator+type+entity+dedup-window bucket), (2) read findings whose alert_emitted flag is still false (the obligation is a query, so it survives a restart), (3) MERGE alerts on a deterministic alert id, (4) mark alert_emitted last. The old presence-based left-anti dedup that permanently suppressed an un-alerted crash survivor is gone; any partial failure retries to exactly one alert per finding while every entity is retained.

findings.title: UEO revisions not bound through FUSE/Confluence/findings/approvals
findings.evidence: Prior session switched UEO writes to a revision-bumping MERGE upsert and added invalidate_revision + _invalidate_findings to WITHDRAW the bound finding when evidence changes. Gate B (B6) proved the FUSE->Confluence->verdict->approval fencing chain end to end: the thread was SEVERED because fuse_results had no revision column (fuse_id was keyed on ueo_id only, so re-fusion at a new revision silently overwrote identity) and confluence_verdicts kept only entity_id, dropping ueo_id/revision so a verdict could not be traced to the finding whose revision the approval binds.
findings.regression: tests/property/test_finding_revision.py + tests/contract/test_revision_thread.py (source: revision is continuous UEO->fuse_results->confluence_verdicts->response_actions; behaviour: an approval binds to the live revision and can_execute refuses once the finding is re-confirmed at a new revision)
findings.fix: fuse_results now carries finding_id + revision (idempotent ADD COLUMNS for existing deployments) and fuse_id is revision-scoped (fuse::{ueo_id}::r{revision}) so each revision's fusion is a distinct row. confluence_verdicts gained ueo_id/finding_id/revision (nullable; the fuse-aware builder populates finding_id from the fuse lineage, the legacy signal-only builder leaves them NULL). The approval layer (response_actions.py + server.py) was already revision-bound; the thread now reaches it.

findings.title: Health could report healthy over a degraded/empty run; _config vs _cfg
findings.evidence: Confirmed a live defect: Monitor.report_health referenced self._cfg while __init__ stored self._config, so every call raised AttributeError, which a bare `except: pass` swallowed -- pipeline_health was never written yet log_complete believed it reported 'healthy'. Fixed self._cfg -> self._config and replaced the silent swallow with logger.exception so a health-write failure is visible. Regression imports the real monitoring module (via an import-boundary pyspark shim) and asserts (1) report_health issues exactly one MERGE into pipeline_health, (2) a failing write is logged at ERROR not swallowed, (3) log_complete drives a health write. This complements the prior-session UEO harvest health work (HEALTHY/DEGRADED/UNAVAILABLE).
findings.regression: tests/property/test_monitor_health.py (write actually lands; failures logged not swallowed; clean=healthy, warning=degraded, error=error, incomplete coverage=degraded, explicit override wins)
findings.fix: log_complete no longer hardcodes "healthy": final status is derived from the worst severity logged during the run (which survives audit-buffer flushes) plus an optional coverage/health signal in details, with an explicit override honored.

findings.title: Tool args ordered by dict insertion; no schema validation before SQL
findings.evidence: Prior session added _validate_and_order_args: orders by parameters.properties and rejects unknown/missing-required/type/enum before spark.sql.
findings.regression: tests/security/test_tool_arg_validation.py (imports the real BaseAgent validators; pins schema-order emission, unknown/missing/type/enum rejection, NULL padding for omitted optionals, and SQL-literal escaping of crafted strings)

findings.title: E2E fixtures/assertions did not isolate executions or hit entry only
findings.evidence: Prior session built an entry-only suite: writes only to Kafka/landing, asserts only on published outputs, 10 required scenarios, per-scenario probe isolation. Offline contract passes; live run BLOCKED pending workspace.

findings.title: Systemic serverless-incompatible streaming/caching APIs across deployed jobs
findings.evidence: When the serverless-API regression was broadened (Gate B) to cover fixed processingTime triggers and DataFrame cache/persist/unpersist, 12 notebooks that the bundle declares on serverless compute were found using classic-only APIs: hardcoded .trigger(processingTime=...) streaming triggers and .cache()/.unpersist(). Serverless streams accept only availableNow/once and do not expose cache/persist. These jobs would fail at runtime on serverless.
findings.regression: tests/contract/test_serverless_notebook_apis.py — each notebook is in the KNOWN_BLOCKED allowlist keyed to H-080 so a NEW violation still fails the suite, and test_known_blocked_notebooks_are_still_blocked prevents the allowlist from rotting once each is migrated.
findings.fix: Gate A (serverless compatibility) resolved this. The seven always-on continuous streaming jobs (enrichment_pipeline, kafka_ingestion, temporal_window_correlator, realtime_graph_cep, typed_bronze_partitioner, lakebase_sync_streaming, ot_protocol_ingestion) were moved from serverless to CLASSIC job clusters in resources/jobs.yml (job_clusters + new_cluster, data_security_mode SINGLE_USER, runtime/node type driven by classic_spark_version and classic_node_type_id bundle variables, pip deps re-declared as task libraries), where continuous processingTime streaming and cache/persist are fully supported. The serverless-scheduled notebooks were made serverless-safe instead: graph_correlation and graph_neighborhood_embeddings had all .cache()/.unpersist() removed, and supply_chain_risk, cloud_posture, detection_confluence and lakebase_sync had their hardcoded .trigger(processingTime=...) replaced with the shared resolve_stream_trigger() helper (added to _shared/delta_helpers.py and exported via bootstrap), which defaults to availableNow. The KNOWN_BLOCKED allowlist in the regression is now empty and both contract tests pass. Live staging validation (databricks bundle validate + a run on classic and serverless compute, and confirming the GraphFrames/classic node types for the target cloud) still requires an authorized workspace.

findings.title: Detectors emit uncalibrated or logically-inverted scores (detector semantics)
findings.evidence: Gate C audited the statistical/ML detectors for math that runs clean but produces wrong scores. Five concrete defects fixed: (F2) Isolation-Forest confidence read abs() of a SIGNED decision_function, so a strongly-NORMAL user scored as anomalous as an attacker; (F4) the beacon detector declared 'periodic' when inter-arrival times were consistent with a UNIFORM distribution (the opposite of a fixed cadence, and failing to reject a null is not evidence for it); (F6) KS-recall similarity normalised the token intersection by the alert length alone (a containment ratio), so a short alert fully inside a long entry scored 1.0 and over-recalled; (F7) Monte-Carlo transition probabilities were perturbed by additive Gaussian noise and compared to a uniform draw WITHOUT clamping, so tail probabilities fired always/never and biased the simulated attack paths; (F9) negative-correlation 'absence' fired on an empty window with no liveness check, so a fresh deploy or ingestion outage tripped every rule at once. Four further issues (self-contaminated UEBA baseline, daily-vs-window baseline scale mismatch, circular 'KS validation', cross-window reuse_ratio / Kleene depth) change a detector's operating point and are deferred to a workspace-backed pass.
findings.regression: tests/property/test_detector_semantics.py (14 tests: pure-helper unit tests for the fixed math + source-scan that each host notebook delegates to the fix and the defective path is gone)
findings.fix: Extracted the fixed math into the pure, importable notebooks/_shared/detector_semantics.py (iforest_anomaly_norm, is_periodic_beacon, clamp_unit, jaccard_similarity), mirroring the calibration.py pattern, and wired each notebook to it. The KS-recall match threshold default moved 0.72 -> 0.4 to match Jaccard's scale (flagged for live re-tuning). The four operating-point issues are recorded, not changed blind.

findings.title: Offline hardening evidence not reproducible; no CI gate; notebook syntax unchecked
findings.evidence: Gate D. The offline evidence lived only in prose and a smoke-test Make target; there was no single command that ran every offline check, and nothing compiled the notebooks (the frontend build does not touch them and the source-extraction tests do not import them). Building the gate immediately caught a real latent regression: 10_fuse_engine.py had an unmatched parenthesis introduced while threading the B6 revision columns, which py_compile flagged.
findings.regression: tools/ci/run_offline_gate.py (py_compile over all 163 notebooks + every tests/**/test_*.py; exits non-zero on any failure) wired into .github/workflows/offline-gate.yml and `make gate-offline`
findings.fix: Added a reproducible offline-gate runner (notebook syntax + full test suite), a CI workflow that runs it plus a manifest-freshness regeneration and the frontend build, a `gate-offline` Make target, and RELEASE_EVIDENCE.md documenting the reproduce steps, gate status (A BLOCKED; B/C/D verified offline) and the explicitly-BLOCKED live gates. Fixed the fuse_engine syntax regression the gate surfaced.
